subject: NicheMapR 1.4 prerelease (please test it out) and a soil moisture paper

messages.author: e46cb5dd353b7dfb
messages.subject: NicheMapR 1.4 prerelease (please test it out) and a soil moisture paper
parts:
Hi everyone,

I've put a pre-release out of the NicheMapR package v1.4. The details of what's included are below, and relate almost entirely to the microclimate model. There are some reasonably large changes, some to the underyling physics to improve predictions of snow cover after some extensive testing against SCAN and SNOTEL sites in the USA. You'll see there are specific functions for the USA and the UK to work with gridded data that are freely available. If some of you can have a play with it and make sure it is working OK, that would be great. Then I'll make the release official.

Also, James Maino and I just published a test of the soil moisture modelling capabilities of the microclimate model in conjunction with new gridded soil products - the following link will give you 50 days of free access to the paper: https://authors.elsevier.com/a/1WxcA52cuJONK

All the best,

Mike


The major aspects of this release include:

  1. A Linux release (!), with thanks to Rafael Schouten for assistance with this.

  2. Functionality to query the SoilGrid database for soil moisture related properties. You'll need to install GSIF and I've had trouble getting this to work on OSX and Ubuntu. See: http://gsif.isric.org/doku.php/wiki:tutorial_soilgrids - if you can get the "REST service for SoilGrids" example going on this page it will work in the microclimate functions. If not you'll have to turn set the flag 'soilgrids' to 0 when you run the microclimate model and specify the soil moisture property vectors (PE, KS, BB, BD) manuall.

  3. A replacement of all references to 'Julian days' with 'Day of Year' (DOY), since technically the former is the number elapsed days since noon on Monday, January 1, 4713 BC (thanks to Tim McVicar for pointing this problem out).

  4. Some substantial revamps to the snow algorithm after extensive testing, including:

  • snow density functions now based on days since snow, rather than DOY, and have kept the original option for a linear function but also added capacity to include the four-parameter exponential function of Sturm et al. 2010 which includes snow depth as a factor too;
  • a new output column in metout/shadmet for snow density so that snow water equivalent can be easily computed;
  • fixed an issue with the way the model captures the phase transition between water and ice in both the snow pack and in the soil, that became apparent when running the model in very cold USA environments - it had a very large impact on soil temperatures, especially their tendency to stabilise near zero degrees C under the snow pack;
  • added heat of fusion to the soil/snow heat budget for when snow is refreezing;
  • the model cannot stably handle snow depths below 2 cm, so added code to save small snow falls until they can make it up to the 2 cm minimum threshold;
  • fixed an issue with relative humidity in the shade at local height not being set properly and possibly exceeding 100%;
  • ensured hourly rainfall forcing data was being used correctly for snow, making sure the melt factor was applied per hour at 1/24th the intensity;
  • infiltration of water into soil under snow now only happens when snow temperature greater than zero (before it was erroneously happening whenever snow was present);
  • made output for soil surface temperature always equal to that of the soil (not the snow skin, as was the case in the previous releases;
  • included both shaded and unshaded snow pack temperature profiles in the output.
  1. Some features to avoid excessive message output from the Fortran program and to kill the simulations if they are getting stuck in an endless loop:
  • added the argument 'message' to suppress integrator messages when it is forced to restart the integration;
  • added argument 'fail' which specifies the upper limit for integrator restarts before quitting to stop situations where there can be endless loops - if the model failed there will be zeros in all rows of the output files from where the problem occurred.

  1. Some beta functions are also included for running the microclimate model via daily forcing data from the NZ NIWA data set, the UK CHESS data set and the USA gridMET data set. The latter two can use opendaps to directly query the online data. Also, there's an opendap connection to the Australian AWAP/AGCD data from 1990-2015. Note that these opendap connections require the 'ncdf4' package which, for Windows, doesn't support opendaps. But, you can install from the compilation at https://github.com/pmjherman/r-ncdf4-build-opendap-windows and it should work.

  2. Changed all real variables in the Fortran code to double precision to reduce integrator error occurrence.

messages.author: 54d4981d6bf68eaf
messages.subject: Re: NicheMapR 1.4 prerelease (please test it out) and a soil moisture paper
parts:
Hi all,

I am finding some difficulties in getting NicheMapR 1.1.4 installed in the latest R version (3.5.0). I have tried installing it in several ways (using install.packages(), with the 'tar.gz' source file, directly form github using install_github()...), but I cannot make it work. In the best case, I succeed in getting the package installed, but I am unable to load it. I get the following message:

Error: package or namespace load failed for ‘NicheMapR’:
 package ‘NicheMapR’ was installed by an R version with different internals; it needs to be reinstalled for use with this R version

It seems that the new version of R has major changes (including internal functions and so on), and is causing this behaviour. I would be really pleased if other NicheMapR users could let me know if they are experiencing the same issue. Alternatively, I would like to know the version of R with which this version of NicheMapR was compiled, to downgrade R, if necessary.

Thank you very much in advance and apologies for any inconvenience,
Urtzi

messages.author: 54d4981d6bf68eaf
messages.subject: Re: NicheMapR 1.4 prerelease (please test it out) and a soil moisture paper
parts:
Dear list,

For those of you that may experience a similar issue, Mike found a solution.

The problem solved when I installed a compatible version of 'gfortran' (available at: https://gcc.gnu.org/wiki/GFortranBinaries#) and re-installed NicheMapR from Mike's repository on github (>devtools::install_github("mrke/NicheMapR")).

Hope this helps someone,

Best wishes,
Urtzi

messages.author: e46cb5dd353b7dfb
messages.subject: Re: NicheMapR 1.4 prerelease (please test it out) and a soil moisture paper
parts:
Hi Simon,

Sadly SoilGrids has stopped working for me. I'm still seeing what might be going wrong. But in the meantime, you can just specify your own soil hydraulic properties like this (based on the data in Campbell and Norman's table 9.1):

library(NicheMapR)
CampNormTbl9_1
          Texture Silt Clay airentry   b      Ks field wilting
1             sand 0.05 0.03      0.7 1.7 5.8e-03  0.09    0.03
2       loamy sand 0.12 0.07      0.9 2.1 1.7e-03  0.13    0.06
3       sandy loam 0.25 0.10      1.5 3.1 7.2e-04  0.21    0.10
4             loam 0.40 0.18      1.1 4.5 3.7e-04  0.27    0.12
5        silt loam 0.65 0.15      2.1 4.7 1.9e-04  0.33    0.13
6  sandy clay loam 0.13 0.27      2.8 4.0 1.2e-03  0.26    0.15
7        clay loam 0.34 0.34      2.6 5.2 6.4e-05  0.32    0.20
8  silty clay loam 0.58 0.33      3.3 6.6 4.2e-05  0.37    0.32
9       sandy clay 0.07 0.40      2.9 6.0 3.3e-05  0.34    0.24
10      silty clay 0.45 0.45      3.4 7.9 2.5e-05  0.39    0.25
11            clay 0.20 0.60      3.7 7.6 1.7e-05  0.40    0.27

soiltype <- 10 # choose a silty clay
BulkDens <- 1 # Mg/m3 peat bog (can go up to .01)
Density <- 2.56 # Mg/m3
PE<-vector() # create empty vector
KS<-vector() # create empty vector
BB<-vector() # create empty vector
BD<-vector() # create empty vector
PE[1:19]<-CampNormTbl9_1[soiltype ,4] #air entry potential J/kg
KS[1:19]<-CampNormTbl9_1[soiltype ,6] #saturated conductivity, kg s/m3
BB[1:19]<-CampNormTbl9_1[soiltype ,5] #soil 'b' parameter
BD[1:19]<-BulkDens # soil bulk density value for soil moisture calcs (Mg/m3)
DD <- rep(Density, 19)

micro<-micro_global(BulkDens = BulkDens, Density = Density, PE = PE, KS = KS, BB = BB, BD = BD, DD = DD)

But note that you should run it for a daily time step if you're interested in soil moisture (which is what these properties are form) and have a year 'spin-up' to let the soil moisture settle down from the initial conditions. E.g.

micro<-micro_global(timeinterval = 365, nyears = 2, BulkDens = BulkDens, Density = Density, PE = PE, KS = KS, BB = BB, BD = BD, DD = DD)

All the best,
Mike

messages.author: 54d4981d6bf68eaf
messages.subject: Re: NicheMapR 1.4 prerelease (please test it out) and a soil moisture paper
parts:
Hi Dirk and Mike,

Good to hear that a brand new version is due soon! Dirk, I would try installing gfortran first, to avoid having to downgrade R and re-install all packages and so on... I have been using NicheMapR this way and I have not found any bug or anything (correct me if I am wrong, Mike).

If you chose to install gfortran, first, you have to go to this link:

https://gcc.gnu.org/wiki/GFortranBinaries#

Then, select your operating system, and download the appropriate file. If you are using a PC I guess that "Official MinGW builds" might be the file for you. After installing that file in your computer, re-install NicheMapR in R by using the next command:

devtools::install_github("mrke/NicheMapR") 

I downloaded the gfortran build for macOS Sierra (10.12) although I am using a mac OS 10.13, and it worked.

Hope this helps.

All the best,
Urtzi
